ca_elixir_wall.blurb: Elixir Wall is a southeast-facing crag in the Rock Creek drainage above Mammoth Lakes, in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 9,000 feet. Ten routes are mostly trad, with a pair of bolted lines, and the grades run from about 5.8 to 5.11 with the bulk in the 5.10 range. A triangular roof marks the left side and an orange headwall stands out in the middle. Sun stays on the face until mid-afternoon, and the spot is quiet and scenic. Getting there means crossing the creek and climbing the hillside beside a talus field, which can be awkward when spring runoff is high.

ca_dragonlance_wall_left_side.blurb: This is the leftward-wrapping section of Dragonlance Wall, part of The Coven near Fawnskin and Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 7,500 feet. It is the first wall you meet on the walk in and faces north and northeast. The ten routes are mostly sport with a handful of trad lines. Grades span an easy walk-up through the 5.8 to 5.10 range to a few hard sport lines in the low to mid 5.12s and 5.13 range. The wall is somewhat complex: some lines begin at the ground and others from ledges higher up the face.

ca_horse_trail_boulders.blurb: Horse Trail Boulders is a small group of limestone boulders in Columbia State Historic Park, in the Sierra Nevada foothills near Sonora. It is one of the easier-to-reach bouldering zones in the park. Ten problems range from V0 up to V6, with most of the volume between V2 and V3, which makes it a good quick session if you want to skip the more adventurous Labyrinth. From the park lot you walk east along a dirt road, pass the Stage Coach Boulders, and turn onto a use trail where most of the blocks sit. Expect poison oak and rattlesnakes.
